items.headline: Google launches Expert Intelligence with more than 100k publisher titles
items.excerpt: Google has launched Expert Intelligence, letting readers use purchased e-books and other trusted sources directly inside its AI products. UK publishers are among the rights holders supplying the initial catalogue of over 100,000 titles.

items.headline: Authors push back as publishers and agents make claims on Anthropic settlement
items.excerpt: As payouts from the $1.5 billion Anthropic copyright settlement begin, authors say publishers and agents appear to be claiming more than their contractual share of the roughly $3,000 owed per infringed work.

items.headline: Authors Guild publishes survey results about copyright registration failures
items.excerpt: Authors ruled ineligible for the Anthropic settlement discovered their publishers never registered their titles with the U.S. Copyright Office — an administrative failure that is now costing writers real money.

items.headline: AI Updates, Remembering Dolly Parton, and More News for Library Workers
items.excerpt: Book Riot's weekly roundup for library workers leads with the latest AI developments hitting libraries — from vendor AI features to policy fights over AI-generated material in collections.

items.headline: How Independent Publishers Can Use AI Drawing Lip Sync to Invite Readers Into a Story
items.excerpt: A how-to for indie publishers on using AI lip-sync animation to give original book illustrations a speaking voice as a promotional on-ramp into the full text.
